properties.name: DEFECT — plan_epoch called on an epoch that already exists resets its status to `planned`, even when only the prose was being revised
properties.statement: Measured on every arrival of increments 430–434 (2026-09-11/12): revising an epoch's description with `plan_epoch` (the constructor's "call again with the same id to revise" path) put the epoch back to `planned`, and it had to be re-arrived with `set_epoch_status`. The constructor's own contract says omitted fields keep their stored value; `status` is not a parameter, so it should be left alone on a revise and only set to `planned` on CREATE. This is the same class as BL-183 (a revise silently un-confirming a status) on a different type, and it is a root-cause fix of a few lines in the temporal slice — not built yet; recorded so it is enduring. Workaround until then: revise the prose FIRST, then `set_epoch_status(arrived)`. Moved here from an agent's machine-local memory file (rule:a-rule-the-project-follows-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-an-agents-memory).
